# Vendor Selection {#sec-vendor-selection}

::: {.callout-note title="Executive summary" appearance="simple"}
- *(Phase C)*
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Drafter guidance" appearance="minimal"}
Target ~5,000 words. See `research/00-book-outline.md` Chapter 9. Open with a real worked example — 80k pages/month of insurance underwriting PDFs with three-month deployment timeline. Walk it live.

## A decision framework

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "Vendor-selection decision tree"
flowchart TD
    A[Start: define use case] --> B{Volume?}
    B -- Low (&lt;10k pages/mo) --> C[Hyperscaler API]
    B -- Medium --> D{Doc variety?}
    B -- High --> E{Self-host?}
    D -- Narrow --> F[Classic IDP or template-based]
    D -- Wide --> G[AI-native specialist]
    E -- Yes --> H[Open-source agentic stack]
    E -- No --> G
```

- The decision is a **stack of four orthogonal questions**: volume, document variability, compliance posture, self-host vs. SaaS.
- Don't start with vendor reviews. Start with these four answers — they collapse the vendor space by ~80%.

## Use-case → architecture mapping

- **High variability, high stakes** (healthcare prior-auth, legal discovery) → Pattern C (hybrid CV+VLM) with HITL gates.
- **High variability, lower stakes** (customer onboarding, mixed-vendor invoices) → Pattern B (agentic loop).
- **Low variability, any stakes** (single-vendor invoices at scale) → Pattern A (single-pass VLM) or classic IDP can still win.
- **Long-form reasoning** (financial filing analysis, multi-doc packets) → Pattern B + downstream reasoning agent. See DABstep — extraction alone is not enough.

## The wrong question to start with

- "Which vendor has the highest benchmark score?" is the wrong starting question.
- The right starting question: **"What is my error budget per output, and what does each error cost me downstream?"**
- Once you have that, vendor selection is just minimizing cost-per-correct-extraction-with-provenance.

## ROI per vertical

### Healthcare prior-auth

- The strongest 2026 ROI case. CMS rule (March 31, 2026) requires public reporting of turnaround/denial/appeal/overturn rates → forcing function for automation.
- Anterior AI + Reducto achieved 99.24% accuracy on prior-auth. The deployment was profitable at any commercial-tier price point because the alternative (manual review at ~30 min/case) was so expensive.
- Pattern C with HITL gates is the de-facto architecture.

### Legal (contract review, discovery)

- ROI varies by sub-domain.
- Contract review: agentic OCR helps with clause extraction, redline detection. Pattern B suffices.
- Discovery: high volume, low per-document stakes (until you find the smoking gun). Often a classic IDP + targeted re-review with agentic OCR.

### Financial services (KYC, loan packets, filings)

- KYC: Pattern B with strong schema validation. Vendors: Reducto, LlamaParse Agentic.
- Loan packets (multi-doc, cross-reference): the DABstep-style challenge. Extraction is necessary but not sufficient. Plan for a separate downstream reasoning layer.
- 10-K / financial filings: LlamaParse Agentic Plus is purpose-built for this.

### Customer onboarding (generic)

- Highest volume, lowest stakes. Cost-per-page matters here.
- Mistral OCR 3 at $1–$2/1k pages is hard to beat for the parsing layer. NuExtract for downstream structured extraction.
- Pattern A or Pattern B; rarely Pattern C.

## The buy-vs-build question

- **Buy the parser, build the eval.** This is the single most important principle in vendor selection.
- Reasons to buy: parsing is mature, vendors have HITL infrastructure you don't want to rebuild, support contracts buy you sleep.
- Reasons to build: data sovereignty hard-requirement, scale where API spend > engineering cost, audit needs that no vendor can satisfy.
- Reasons to **always build your own eval**: only you know what "correct" means for your documents. No vendor's golden set matches yours.

## A shortlist methodology

- Pick three vendors across three tiers (one AI-native, one hyperscaler, one classic IDP or open-source).
- Run all three on your golden set (200–500 hand-labeled documents from production).
- Score on the metric that matches your downstream cost (Chapter 11 on metric selection).
- Decide on data, not demos.

## Named takes

> *"Most teams pick a vendor before they pick a metric. This is backwards. Choose the metric that determines your downstream cost, then choose the vendor that minimizes that metric."*

> *"Build-vs-buy is the wrong frame. Buy the parser, build the eval. Reuse vendor parsers; never reuse vendor evals."*
